material_review.review_method: Read actual synthesis, final principal report and adopted claims, original factual result and metric view, original report audits, exact fact/support/scope bindings. No paid reviewer, investigator rewrite, or new scientific computation.

adopted_claims.statement: The historical official reach outcome for this archived execution is recorded as not accepted, and the recorded failure is a finite terminal position offset rather than a solver fault.
The recorded sampled holding criteria fail: the sampled position error exceeds its position threshold and the sampled tip speed exceeds its speed threshold over the recorded sampling window.

The archived independent recomputation for the reach, holding position and holding speed criteria is available with empty missing material yet reports a false recomputed result, that is, an available failed criterion rather than absent recomputation.
The archived execution was valid and complete without solver or force-bound faults, so the recorded non-acceptance is not attributable to solver errors or force violations.

The recorded timing places the measured mean complete update time and the total measured computation time far above the nominal control period, with every recorded control update counted as a deadline miss and real time not demonstrated; these are measured or computed values, not capability guarantees.
The archived execution is recorded as valid and complete with zero force-bound violations and zero solver errors, so the recorded limits are timing and settling rather than solver or force faults.

The archived one-step prediction summary covers aligned world-frame first-step predictions with small mean and maximum tip differences and no missing entries, and its own scope limits it to accepted first-step predictions matched to the next execution timestamp with no future-plan replay comparison, so it is neither reach nor holding acceptance.

The holding record rests on sampled evidence without a continuous-time guarantee, and the recorded official result stands because unavailable independent recomputation does not erase a recorded official result.
